title: Roomba mode exists: the arena, the task, and its known answer
question: Stage two opens: can the measured robot locomote, bounce, and fill space in a 3D sim — and what coverage does a hand-coded bouncer set as the bar?
headline: The 3D model (independent wheels, yaw, walled arena) balances and locomotes; the scripted bounce controller — hub-realizable observations only — covers 10-12% of the arena per 40 s episode. That is the known answer a learned exploration policy must beat. Building it replayed run 6 in 3D: the speed term is load-bearing, and clamping it fells the robot in seconds.

media.bouncer_overhead.mp4: scripted bounce baseline, overhead camera, 40 s: cruise, wall hit, back off, turn, repeat

hub_output: -- sim; baseline over 6 x 40 s episodes --
coverage mean ~10-12% (10x10 grid), most episodes survive, occasional wall fall
pitch+rate only: falls 5/5 -- the speed term is load-bearing in 3D as on hardware (run 6)
speed-term authority clamped to 0.15: falls every episode within ~2 s
per-wheel traction ~0.08 N*m before slip; whipsaw limit cycle if the velocity loop is aggressive
